summary: Iter-10 Resend email integration + /admin/orders/{id}/ship fully validated. 10/10 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_v10_email.py pass (regression + email flows + admin ship). Graceful-degradation path verified out-of-band by blanking RESEND_API_KEY, restarting backend, creating an order — order returned 200 and logs emitted 'Resend not configured, skipping email to ocepjos@gmail.com' twice (order_confirmation + admin_new_order). Env restored afterwards.
critical_code_review_comments: email_service._send uses resend.api_key module-global assignment per call — fine for current single-worker setup, but if multiple async tasks ran concurrently with different keys it would race. Current env has single RESEND_API_KEY so non-issue.

admin.py POST /orders/{id}/ship returns 200 with {ok:false, error:'Order tidak ditemukan'} on missing order instead of HTTP 404. Functional and consistent with sibling update_status endpoint, but inconsistent with REST conventions — spec explicitly requested this shape so accepted.

payment.py webhook uses asyncio.create_task(send_payment_success(...)) WITHOUT keeping a reference; if the event loop is busy at shutdown, the task could be GC'd. In practice (FastAPI long-lived loop) the fire-and-forget is fine, but storing the task handle in a module-level set would be more defensive.
server.py uses FastAPI BackgroundTasks for order emails — correct non-blocking pattern. admin.py and payment.py use asyncio.create_task instead (no BackgroundTasks access there) — also valid.
email_service._send catches broad Exception and logs at ERROR — good, callers (BackgroundTasks/create_task) never see exceptions.
email_service.render_admin_notification WhatsApp phone normalization: the `elif not wa_phone.startswith('62')` branch is a no-op (assigns wa_phone to itself). Minor dead code — safe but noisy.

No unit test coverage for the HTML renderers themselves; behavior-driven log assertions suffice given the test-mode Resend sandbox. If future iterations add template variants, consider snapshot-testing render_* outputs.
